title: Eliminated variable formula
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, f : Fin r → A, and i : Fin r. Let I = (∑ j, f(j)X_j − 1) in A[X_j : j : Fin r] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], B its quotient, Af the localization at f(i), Bf the localization of B at the image of f(i) [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and x_j the localized class of X_j. Give Bf its induced Af-algebra structure [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property]. For any Af-algebra equivalence e : Af[Y_j : j ≠ i] ≃ Bf whose forward map is evaluation at x_j and whose inverse sends x_j to Y_j for j ≠ i, its inverse sends x_i to f(i)⁻¹(1−∑ j ≠ i f(j)Y_j).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve): 'B_{f_i} is smooth over A_{f_i}. Details omitted.' (the isomorphism is the omitted detail)

proof.text: The generator of I belongs to I, so its quotient class is zero. Map this identity into Bf, rewrite coefficients using IsLocalization.map_eq, and separate the i term with Fintype.sum_eq_add_sum_subtype_ne. Apply e.symm, using coefficient commutation and the assumed inverse values on the other variables. Solve the resulting linear equation by multiplying by C(invSelf(f(i))), using IsLocalization.Away.mul_invSelf.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\ge1$, $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ and $1\le i\le r$. Put
$$
B=A[X_1,\dots,X_r]\Big/\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^rf_jX_j-1\Bigr),
$$
let $A_{f_i}=A[1/f_i]$, and let $B_{f_i}$ be the localization of $B$ at the image of $f_i$,
an $A_{f_i}$-algebra via the map induced by $A\to B$. Write $x_j\in B_{f_i}$ for the image of
$X_j$. Let
$$
\varphi\colon A_{f_i}[Y_j : j\ne i]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }B_{f_i}
$$
be any isomorphism of $A_{f_i}$-algebras that is the evaluation homomorphism
$Y_j\mapsto x_j$ $(j\ne i)$ and satisfies $\varphi^{-1}(x_j)=Y_j$ for every $j\ne i$. Then
$$
\varphi^{-1}(x_i)=f_i^{-1}\Bigl(1-\sum_{j\ne i}f_jY_j\Bigr).
$$

proof.text:
The class of $\sum_jf_jX_j-1$ in $B$ is zero, so $\sum_{j=1}^rf_jx_j=1$ in $B_{f_i}$, with the
coefficients $f_j$ read in $A_{f_i}$. Separating the $i$-th term gives
$f_ix_i+\sum_{j\ne i}f_jx_j=1$. Apply $\varphi^{-1}$, which is $A_{f_i}$-linear and sends
$x_j$ to $Y_j$ for $j\ne i$:
$$
f_i\,\varphi^{-1}(x_i)+\sum_{j\ne i}f_jY_j=1.
$$
Since $f_i$ is a unit of $A_{f_i}$, multiplying by $f_i^{-1}$ gives
$\varphi^{-1}(x_i)=f_i^{-1}\bigl(1-\sum_{j\ne i}f_jY_j\bigr)$.
